# Oktoviano Gandhi

> Dr Oktoviano (Okto) Gandhi is a solar PV and power systems specialist: floating solar PV, battery energy storage systems (BESS), grid integration and ancillary services, solar forecasting, PV performance, and techno-economics, mostly in Southeast Asia. Scientist at the Qatar Environment and Energy Research Institute (QEERI), Hamad Bin Khalifa University; previously eleven years at the Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS), National University of Singapore; co-founder of Alva Energi, Indonesia. Indonesian; works in English, Indonesian, and Malay.

Key facts: feasibility studies for more than 7 GWp of PV and 1 GWh of battery storage (ADB, World Bank, IDB, USAID, and private clients); maintained the SERIS Global Floating PV Database (about 1,700 projects in 66 countries, 2022 to 2026); one of three main authors of GIZ studies for Indonesia's Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources on ancillary services and on battery storage regulation, and a financial model for the ministry to test draft benchmark prices for PV and battery storage; led PV grid integration in Singapore's national solar forecasting programme for the Energy Market Authority and Singapore Power (2019 to 2022); more than 50 peer-reviewed publications with more than 3,000 citations; PhD, National University of Singapore; MPhys, University of Oxford.

## Expertise

- [Floating solar PV](https://ogandhi.com/expertise/floating-pv/): Where floating PV makes sense, what it costs compared with ground-mounted PV, and how to take a reservoir, lagoon, or coastal site from screening to feasibility.
- [Battery energy storage (BESS)](https://ogandhi.com/expertise/battery-storage/): Where batteries add value in a power system, how to size and dispatch them, and how regulation, contracts, and prices can make storage projects bankable.
- [Grid integration, ancillary services, and regulation](https://ogandhi.com/expertise/grid-integration/): How much solar PV and battery storage a power system can take, which integration measures cost least, and how regulation and markets can make them happen.
- [Solar forecasting and its value](https://ogandhi.com/expertise/solar-forecasting/): What a better solar forecast is worth to markets, system operators, and plant owners, and how to produce forecasts that quantify their own uncertainty.
- [PV performance and technology choice](https://ogandhi.com/expertise/pv-performance/): Which modules, mounting structures, and trackers give the lowest cost of electricity at a given site, and how climate, albedo, and dust change the answer.
- [Feasibility and techno-economics](https://ogandhi.com/expertise/techno-economics/): Levelised costs, tariffs, and financial returns for PV and battery projects, and the engineering assumptions that drive them.
- [Off-grid, island, and hybrid power systems](https://ogandhi.com/expertise/off-grid-and-islands/): Moving diesel-powered island and remote grids to solar PV and batteries without losing reliability, and keeping village power systems working for years after installation.
